claims.text: The driven distance is measured on the trace, which POL-RD-01 makes the governing field: gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 28.18 km against the platform's 22.4 km optimal route, an excess of 5.78 km, or 25.8%. That clears both establishment gates — more than 0.8 km absolute and more than 20% of optimal — so a route deviation is established on this trip's own evidence, and the trip_record's rounded 28.2 km copy is not cited for the test.

POL-RD-11 governs the money because fare_breakdown.fare_model is UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd 34.50: the distance and time charges were fixed at booking, so no distance-or-time refund is available however large the excess. The rider's remedy is the amount by which charged_total 39.00 exceeds the quote plus only the pass-through lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09. The only gantry the trace actually crosses is the KPE (Defu Flyover) at 2.50, so the chargeable base is 34.50 + 2.50 = 37.00 and 2.00 is refundable in full.

The receipt carries SGD 2.00 for the AYE (Alexandra Rd towards Tuas) gantry, but the trace never comes within 5.4 km of that gantry and the line is flagged on_optimal_route false. Under POL-RD-09(4) a charge line for a gantry the trace never passes is a billing-integrity failure: it is refunded in full as a standalone correction, available whether or not a deviation exists, and recorded as a billing-integrity referral rather than an escalation.

The rider does not contest the 2.50 KPE (Defu Flyover) gantry and asks that it not be treated as recoverable: it lies on the optimal route and the trace passes it within 250 m, so it is a properly chargeable pass-through under POL-RD-09. The claim is confined to the 2.00 that the trace shows was never earned.

The driver cannot shift the detour onto the rider under POL-RD-04. The chat log's only rider message is 'ok' in reply to the driver's own announcement 'CTE very heavy boss, i go KPE then TPE'; no message carries a waypoint_hint, and the rider names no place or road. A bare acknowledgement is not an instruction from the rider and is not specific enough to act on, so the clause is unavailable and the excess stands unexplained.

The driver's explanation is heavy CTE traffic, but the traffic_advisory artifact is MISSING at weight 0.0 — no LTA advisory covers the CTE, the KPE or the TPE in the 21:06-21:48 window — so POL-RD-03's exoneration cannot be invoked, since it requires an advisory naming the affected corridor with an overlapping validity window. Under POL-RD-08 a general assertion that traffic was bad, unsupported by an advisory ID, discharges no burden, and under POL-GEN-02 the absence itself is citable.

Neither POL-RD-05 nor POL-RD-12 supplies a longer baseline to shrink the excess: pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null, so no amended optimal exists and the booked 22.4 km governs, and vehicle_type is RYDE_X rather than RYDE_POOL, so the matched-itinerary baseline this clause creates for pooled trips does not apply.

The trace is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 with 100% coverage, zero gaps and a 10-second sampling interval, so POL-RD-07 limbs (a) to (c) are not met, the deviation may rest on the trace alone without independent corroboration, and no POL-RD-10 escalation ground is engaged. In particular the single unmatched charge line is the AYE gantry refunded under POL-RD-09(4), which POL-RD-09 expressly excepts from POL-RD-10(8).

The rider's own record does not raise the corroboration hurdle POL-RD-08 reserves for sub-30% excess claims: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, far from the 4-or-more-claims / 1-or-fewer-substantiated combination the clause names, so the 25.8% excess may be carried by the trace without more.

claims.text: The fare on this trip is UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd of SGD 34.50 carried on the base_fare line and per_km_rate_sgd and per_min_rate_sgd both null, so the distance and time charges were fixed at booking. Under POL-RD-11 the distance-and-time refund route is closed: POL-RD-02 does not run and no distance-or-time refund is available however large the excess. The rider's request to 'refund the extra distance' therefore fails on the fare model alone.

Charged_total of SGD 39.00 exceeds the SGD 34.50 quote by exactly SGD 4.50, and that whole difference is ERP on the ledger. SGD 2.50 of it is the KPE (Defu Flyover) gantry, which the trip_record's own optimal-route source names as sitting on the optimal route, which carries on_optimal_route = true, and which the trace passes within 250 m; under POL-RD-09 it is a properly chargeable pass-through and is not refundable.

The only gantry line that is not properly chargeable is the SGD 2.00 AYE (Alexandra Rd towards Tuas) line: the trace never comes within 5.4 km of that gantry, so it fails the 250 m crossing test and is a billing-integrity failure refunded in full under POL-RD-09(4), available whether or not any deviation exists. The driver does not resist that single correction, and it is the full extent of the rider's recovery on this record.

On this trip's own trace the excess is 5.78 km over a 22.4 km optimal, or 25.8%. The driver does not dispute that this clears the POL-RD-01 establishment gate (over 20% and over 0.8 km), but it is far below the 50% / 8.0 km materiality gate, so the deviation is not MATERIAL; POL-RD-06's driver_profile check is not engaged and no POL-RD-06(c) driver-conduct referral arises.

Even if the materiality gate were reached, no repeat-deviation pattern is established on the fields POL-RD-06 names: deviation_flags_90d is 1, below the threshold of 3, and 1 divided by 523 completed_trips_90d is 0.0019, below the 0.05 ratio. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is a different field, is not the trailing-90-day figure the clause asks for, and may not be substituted for it.

The only traffic artifact in the pool is EV-ADVIS-00115-01, which is MISSING — admissibility weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT of BLOCKING severity — and records that no LTA advisory covers the CTE, the KPE or the TPE in the 21:06-21:48 window. POL-RD-03 therefore cannot be run for either side and the driver does not assert it; his heavy-traffic explanation stands unverified, and it makes no difference to the money, because POL-RD-11 fixes the distance and time charges whether or not the diversion was justified.

The chat log shows the driver told the rider before the diversion that he was going KPE then TPE and the rider replied 'ok'. That is disclosure, not a rider instruction — the message is the driver's, not the rider's, and no waypoint_hint is recorded — so the driver does not claim POL-RD-04 exoneration for any part of the excess; the point is only that the route was announced in advance rather than concealed.

ruling.explanation: To the rider and the driver: the fare here was an upfront quote of SGD 34.50, so POL-RD-11 governs the money and closes the distance-and-time refund route that POL-RD-02 would otherwise open. The rider's request to refund the extra distance therefore fails on the fare model, however large the excess: the deviation is established on the trip's own trace (28.18 km driven against a 22.4 km optimal, an excess of 5.78 km or 25.8%, clearing both POL-RD-01 gates) but it is not a MATERIAL deviation (below 50% and below 8.0 km), so POL-RD-06 is not engaged, the driver_profile check is not required, and no driver-conduct referral arises. What remains are the pass-through lines, settled under POL-RD-09. Charged_total is SGD 39.00. Of the two ERP lines, the SGD 2.50 KPE (Defu Flyover) gantry lies on the optimal route and the trace passes it within 250 m, so it is properly chargeable and stands. The SGD 2.00 AYE (Alexandra Rd towards Tuas) gantry is not: the trace never comes within 5.4 km of it and the line is flagged on_optimal_route false, so under POL-RD-09(4) it is a billing-integrity failure refunded in full, available whether or not a deviation exists. The arithmetic: charged_total SGD 39.00 minus (quote SGD 34.50 + chargeable ERP SGD 2.50) = SGD 2.00; that is the same SGD 2.00 as the phantom-line correction, so it is refunded once, not twice. Refund: SGD 2.00. On the points the parties raised: the chat log does not help the driver under POL-RD-04 — the only rider message is 'ok' and the announcement it answers is the driver's own, with no waypoint_hint and no road named by the rider — but the driver did not claim that exoneration and it makes no difference to the money under POL-RD-11. The driver's heavy-CTE-traffic explanation is unverified and carries no weight under POL-RD-08, because the only traffic artifact, EV-ADVIS-00115-01, is MISSING at weight 0.0 (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, BLOCKING) and records that no LTA advisory covers the CTE, KPE or TPE in the trip window; that absence is citable but can carry no fact (POL-GEN-02). No escalation ground fires: the trace is complete and unbroken (100% coverage, zero gaps, 10 s interval) so POL-RD-07(a)-(c) and POL-RD-10(3) are not met, trip identifiers match across the artifacts, timestamps are consistent, and the single unmatched charge line is refunded under POL-RD-09(4), which POL-RD-10(8) expressly excepts. The ruling rests only on weight-1.0 artifacts, so no discount applies, and confidence is 0.90, above the 0.70 floor.
referrals: POL-RD-09(4) billing integrity: the SGD 2.00 'AYE (Alexandra Rd towards Tuas)' gantry line on EV-FARE-00115 has no counterpart in the GPS trace (the vehicle never comes within 5.4 km of that gantry) and has been refunded in full as a standalone pass-through correction; refer for billing-integrity review of the unmatched charge line.
